transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, occupational health at my job sent me here. They're saying my weight is dangerously low, especially for someone running presses and doing fabrication work all day. I mean, I honestly just thought I was getting leaner and more disciplined with myself, but they wouldn't let it go. So, here I am.
Are you afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat?
Yeah, I am. I mean... if the scale goes up even just a little bit, I panic. I just worry that I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so hard for, and... and end up heavy again.
Do you deliberately limit how much food you eat in order to prevent gaining weight?

Yes, I do. Most days, I keep it to just coffee before I head in for the early shift. Then at lunch, I'll have maybe half a protein bar. And later, after yoga, just a small bowl of vegetables. That's really it. If I eat more than that... I don't know, the whole day just feels completely out of control.
Have healthcare professionals told you that your current weight is significantly below what is healthy for your height?

Yes, like I mentioned when we first started talking, the nurses at occupational health told me exactly that. They said my weight is dangerously low, especially for someone running presses and doing fabrication work all day on the floor. I honestly just thought I was getting leaner and... and more disciplined with my routine. But yeah, they are the ones who said it's too low and made me come in here.
Have you had episodes when you felt unable to control your eating and ate an unusually large amount of food?

No, I haven't. I don't really ever eat a large amount of food, and I definitely don't lose control like that. Like I said, I'm pretty strict about keeping it to just the coffee, half a protein bar, and some vegetables. I don't have times where I just eat and eat.
